theme_overview.vibe: Modern, professional, clean, corporate, mechanical, highly functional ERP.
theme_overview.theme_preference: Light mode primary for day-to-day workshop use, with an optional Dark mode toggle for low-light environments. Not overly colorful—color is strictly used for data visualization, status badging, and primary actions.

headings.description: A neo-grotesque sans-serif. Gives a slightly mechanical, engineered, and solid corporate feel without being overly stylized. Great for a dashboard.

body.description: Excellent legibility for dense tables, tabular data, and forms. Superb support for Turkish characters (İ, Ğ, Ü, Ş, Ö, Ç).

monospace.description: To be used exclusively for License Plates, VIN numbers, Service Order IDs, and part numbers.

primary.description: Deep Industrial Slate. Used for primary typography, sidebar backgrounds, and structural elements.

accent.description: Signal Orange. Mechanical and highly visible. Used sparingly for primary CTA buttons (e.g., 'Yeni Servis Kaydı') and active state indicators.

visual_enhancers.borders_and_radius: Subtle border radiuses. Use `rounded-md` (6px) or `rounded-lg` (8px). Avoid fully rounded pill shapes except for status badges. UI must feel sharp, structured, and technical.
visual_enhancers.shadows: Very subtle, crisp shadows. Use `shadow-sm` for cards, `shadow-md` for dropdowns/modals. No glowing shadows.
visual_enhancers.textures: Flat and solid. Avoid gradients unless necessary for specific chart data. The interface must prioritize clarity over decoration.

layouts.app_structure: Left fixed sidebar (`w-64`), Top fixed header (`h-16`) containing global search (Plaka, Şasi, Müşteri) and user profile. Main content area fills remaining space with standard `p-6` or `p-8` padding.
layouts.dashboard_grid: High-density bento mode. 4-column grid (`grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4`). Top row: 4 KPI summary cards (`col-span-1`). Middle row: Revenue Chart (`col-span-3`) + Status Donut (`col-span-1`). Bottom row: Latest Services table (`col-span-4`).
layouts.tables: Dense styling (`py-2 px-3` cells). Zebra striping or subtle `hover:bg-slate-50` for rows. Stick to white backgrounds with 1px `border-slate-200` around the table container.

interactive_motorcycle_diagram.instruction: Create an interactive SVG diagram of a motorcycle side profile. Define clickable zones (`path` or `g` elements) for Front Brake, Rear Brake, Engine, Transmission, Exhaust, Electric, Battery, Fuel System, Suspension. On click, toggle a red highlight fill (e.g., `fill-red-500/50`) to mark damaged/faulty zones. Must be part of the 'Service Order Creation' flow.

motorcycle_type_illustrations.instruction: Use simple, clean vector-style SVGs or distinct icons for different motorcycle types (Scooter, Naked, Sport, Touring, Adventure, Enduro, Cross, Chopper, Cruiser, Cafe Racer, Electric). Display these in the 'Motorcycle Details' card.

forms.instruction: Use Shadcn UI forms. Align labels to the top of inputs. Use 2-column grids for long forms (e.g., Customer or Service Order creation).

sidebar.instruction: Dark mode styling (`bg-slate-900 text-slate-300`). Active links should have white text and a Signal Orange (`bg-orange-500`) left border indicator.

icons.usage: Use Phosphor Icons (Regular or Duotone weight) for clear, technical, and dense dashboard iconography.

motion.interactions: Minimalist and snappy. `duration-150 ease-in-out` for all hover states. No bouncy animations.
motion.page_transitions: Fade-in only (`opacity-0` to `opacity-100`). No complex entrance staggers for data tables to avoid slowing down the user.

accessibility.contrast: Ensure 4.5:1 minimum for all text. The status badges must use dark text over light backgrounds to ensure readability.
accessibility.testing: All interactive and key informational elements MUST include a `data-testid` attribute (e.g., `data-testid="btn-create-service-order"`, `data-testid="input-plate-number"`).
accessibility.localization: Ensure proper display of TL (₺) currency symbol, DD.MM.YYYY dates, and 24h time format.

motorcycle_placeholder.description: Motorcycle parked on the side. Good for placeholder when a customer's specific motorcycle photo isn't uploaded.

mechanic_avatar.description: Mechanic working in garage. Good for default technician avatar or dashboard background element.

universal_guidelines_for_main_agent: You tend to converge toward generic, 'on distribution' outputs. In frontend design, this creates what users call the 'AI slop' aesthetic. Avoid this: make creative, distinctive frontends that surprise and delight.
Dark colors look good when used independently without gradients. DO NOT use dark colors as gradients
Don't make generic centered layouts, simplistic gradients, and uniform styling.
Create depth through layered design elements with z-index hierarchy
Use glass-morphism effects with backdrop filters (12-24px blur) only where appropriate (e.g., sticky headers), but NOT for data-heavy dashboard tables.
You MUST NOT apply universal transition. Eg: transition: all. This results in breaking transforms. Always add transitions for specific interactive elements like button, input excluding transforms.
You MUST NOT center align the app container, ie do not add .App { text-align: center; } in the css file. This disrupts the human natural reading flow of text.
Always use modern button styles like pill-shaped, or sharp button with interaction animations & color relevant to the app style.
NEVER: use AI assistant Emoji characters like 🤖🧠💭💡🔮🎯 etc for icons.
Every interaction needs micro-animations - hover states, transitions, parallax effects, and entrance animations. Static = dead.
Use 2-3x more spacing than feels comfortable. Cramped designs look cheap.
Subtle grain textures, noise overlays, custom cursors, selection states, and loading animations: separates good from extraordinary.
Main agent relies on these image URLs. Missing categories (especially sponsor logos) = main agent will use placeholder text which is FORBIDDEN
Prioritize using pre-existing components from src/components/ui when applicable.
Create new components that match the style and conventions of existing components when needed.
Examine existing components to understand the project's component patterns before creating new ones.
Use sonner for toasts. Sonner component are located in /app/src/components/ui/sonner.tsx
